The Manufacturing Supervisor Leadership Program

Most training fades within weeks. This one doesn't. It is a step-by-step, habit-changing system that your own supervisors run every day, The safe way is simply the way things are done around here.

Supervisors become effective trainers just by pressing play.

At least 3 times a week they show their team a 3-5 minute video on one technique that is used when they are working. The video is designed to influence the workers to understand why it makes them feel better . The video does all the training for the supervisor

Supervisors become effective at teaching Leadership Skills

Twice a month, the supervisors learn a new leadership skill by looking at a 15 minute video that trains them. The leadership skills are easy for the supervisor to learn, implement and maintain with their teams. They are designed to be fun for the workers and they have powerful effects on the teams performance.

Supervisors learn to recognize and reward workers who are “caught” using safe habits.

They give a reward to any worker they see doing a stretch, lifting, pushing or pulling properly, or helping another worker. Workers feel good because they were complimented, and they are influenced to do good things when there is no supervisor around.

The way you impact peoples behavior when you are not around, is by the way you treat them when you are around.

The Best stretching program

Every worker is taught a stretching routine. Each stretch is designed to reduce tension, ache or fatigue, in one part of the body and create more energy to make work easier. They are asked to perform one 3 breath stretch twice per hour. They choose which stretch to do based on how they feel at the moment. Since 2012, most workers are still doing them for years. Why? Because they feel better.

Available to any manufacturer

On-Site Risk Evaluation and Written Report

The most common cause of injury, pain, and lost productivity in manufacturing is also the easiest to miss: poor posture while working. It looks harmless, and it costs plants a great deal. Dr. Carlin comes to your facility to find it, along with the other risks hiding in your equipment, ergonomics, procedures, and worker habits.

How it works:

  1. Before the visit: Your workforce completes an anonymous survey. It reveals what people won't always say out loud, and it prepares them for Dr. Carlin's visit.
  2. During the visit: Dr. Carlin walks your floor with a well-liked, respected worker or supervisor and talks with people in many short, informal interviews.
  3. After the visit: You receive a written report organized by department. For each department, it lists the risks observed, the problems they can cause, and practical solutions, both purchased and, when possible, low-cost ones you can make yourselves.
  4. Support afterward: Dr. Carlin is available to speak with whoever is making the physical corrections.
Investment: $5,000 plus expenses (travel, lodging, and a reasonable per diem)
